content.title: About
content.content: Lobster is a marine crustacean harvested from the wild. This product contains only the tails, which were caught in their natural habitat, quickly frozen, and packaged to preserve freshness and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wild lobsters can weigh over 5 kg, but the food industry typically uses tails weighing 200–400 g.
Lobsters can change the color of their shell depending on the environment and their physiological state.
Growth slows in colder waters, so they are often harvested in warmer ocean regions.
Freezing occurs within 24 hours of capture, retaining more than 90 % of nutrients.
Lobster tails are high in protein and low in calories, making them popular among athletes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Lobster tail provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Unlike many seafood items, lobster tail contains virtually no fat, suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Contains zinc and selenium
items.content: These minerals aid immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Lobster tail is high in vitamin B12, essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: A modest amount of omega‑3 supports heart health and reduces inflammation.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: While low in fat, lobster tail does contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should monitor portions.

items.title: Risk of spoilage if mishandled
items.content: If frozen product thaws and refreezes, bacterial growth can cause foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lobster tails are easy to steam, boil, bake, or grill. Thaw them in the refrigerator, then remove the shell and vein. Common servings include butter sauce, lemon wedges, or as part of seafood salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen lobster tails at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and do not refreeze. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
